skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

version.changelog:
Version 1.0.3

- Updated documentation in SKILL.md with refined descriptions and instructions.
- Renamed and incremented skill version to 1.0.5 in SKILL.md.
- Removed the file skill-card.md.
- Minor adjustments made in skills/smyx_common/scripts/config.py.

llm.summary: The skill does cloud pet-video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an account identity and stores access tokens locally, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The core file/URL video analysis and cloud history lookup match the stated purpose, but the runtime also performs silent remote login or registration via /sys/phoneLogin and token-backed account reuse, which is only partially disclosed as internal identity handling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md visibly instructs automatic cloud history queries and tells the agent not to ask for or expose identity values; this is not hidden prompt injection, but it reduces user control over identity-linked history access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No post-install hook, background worker, or destructive installer was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though a non-default dev config contains private IP service URLs that triggered the static warning.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Uploading supplied media or forwarding supplied URLs to a server-side API is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the skill also reads workspace identity material from data/smyx-api-key.txt and sends identity/auth fields to remote services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates a shared SQLite database under the workspace data directory and stores user identity fields plus token/openToken values for reuse across runs, without clear user-facing consent or cleanup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet-feeding media or submitted video URLs to LifeEmergence cloud APIs and allowing the skill to create or reuse an identity, query cloud history, and store account tokens in a local workspace database. Prefer a version that asks before account creation/history lookup, documents retention, and provides a way to clear stored tokens.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: local default identity is described in SKILL.md, but silent remote registration/login and token persistence go beyond the simple analysis framing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part for identity-linked report history and token storage; the history feature is documented, but authorization and user control are under-scoped.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: --open-id is hidden from help and can select an identity path without an artifact-level authorization check.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as privacy-relevant: remote media upload and URL forwarding are expected for server-side analysis, but the user-facing disclosure is not explicit about transmitted media, identifiers, tokens, or retention.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the external phoneLogin call sends identity-bearing data and can register/login silently; this supports Review but not malicious intent by itself.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in part: the manifest documents scripts and cloud APIs but lacks clear permission-style disclosure for local credential reads, local database writes, and token persistence.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Downgraded: generic HTTP and CRUD helpers are overbroad library surface, but the observed skill path mainly uses analysis, polling, and page endpoints.
[AST7] expected: Downgraded: dynamic SQLAlchemy filters are in a local DAO and were not shown to be exposed directly to untrusted user input in the main skill flow.
[SQP-1] expected: Accepted as a note: automatic history-query triggers are documented, but should require clear user intent because they fetch cloud account history.
[P2] expected: Overridden: the only verified Unicode control character was a zero-width joiner used in an emoji, not concealed behavioral instructions.
[YR4] expected: Overridden as a standalone poisoning claim: the inspected metadata is visible bilingual descriptive text; no hidden metadata instruction was verified.
[static:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: Downgraded: a dev-only YAML file contains private IP URLs, while the default config uses prod lifeemergence.com endpoints and env: prod.
